summary: First-principles design review, iteration 8, executed in the campaign worktree — the lineage that will launch the GPU runs (full record in review_loop/scrutiny_08.md). The central finding required no code reading: the experiment infrastructure had FORKED. The campaign branch (holding run_campaign.py, the launch button) diverged at iteration 3 and lacked every iteration-4-7 fix: the H1->H2 hierarchical confirmatory family and sign-flip power floor (iter 4), the eval-record completeness rewrite (iter 5 — the branch had only its own earlier draft, missing the greedy-keyed pass@1 and loader-consistency corrections), the predictions-producer completeness fix whose pro-treatment k-deflation was confirmed on 5/10 real pilot instances (iter 6), and the fork-decision draw accounting including the Submitted-at-injection data-loss fix (iter 7). Scrutiny iterations 6 and 7 both listed 'rebase the campaign worktree before launch' as a required action; it had not happened — a launch from this branch would have produced headline artifacts violating every completeness guarantee the design documents promise, with the iteration-6 bias favoring the treatment. FIXED: merged the iteration-4-7 branch into this one (single conflict resolved by taking the iteration-5+ eval driver, a verified strict superset of the campaign draft); all 102 merged tests passed immediately. Beyond the merge, four further substantive findings, all fixed and tested: (1) R6.3's cross-arm fairness comparison was INCOMPUTABLE on the control arm — budget_audit.py's discovery globs matched only the treatment layout while the control nests each resample at <iid>/run<idx>/<iid>/, so the audit returned n_instances=0 exactly on the arm where the 'control receives at least as much compute' inequality could fail; the campaign driver audited only the treatment while its docstring claimed both arms. Fixed with layout auto-detection + draw records keyed by the predictions tid run<idx> (crashed metadata-less resamples disclosed via n_draws_missing_metadata), a budget_audit_control campaign step, both-arm commands in RESULTS SS5, and an R6.3 amendment requiring stage-tested both-arm support; treatment numbers verified byte-identical on the pilot (53 trajectories / 12,882,383 tokens). (2) The campaign's LLM analyst — which adaptively chooses follow-up cells from interim data — was pinned to the ITERATION-3 design (its prompt cited scrutiny_03 only, pre-H1/H2, no power floor, no saturation or productivity reading rules); repointed at the current design with explicit reading rules, test-pinned. (3) The adaptivity itself was undisclosed adaptive data collection: harmless for the confirmatory cell (Phase A runs first, exactly once, before any analyst call — structurally enforced and tested) but the strategy_t0.7_seed2 repeat cell invited optional stopping. New R6.5 adaptive-execution-boundary clause: the FIRST completed Phase A run is the confirmatory dataset, repeats are variance-only, decisions are checked-in artifacts, and the data-dependent exploratory cell set is disclosed (RESULTS SS2.2 paragraph). (4) Two integrity holes in the campaign runner: the standing vLLM container's model was never verified against the config (added a demonstrable-mismatch-only preflight via /v1/models), and the analyst runs with permissions skipped but nothing enforced its 'make no other changes' instruction (added a porcelain-diff tree-integrity check that stops the campaign if anything outside campaign_decisions/results changed). Also re-verified iteration 7's queued fork-path questions (KeyboardInterrupt mid-fork, trajectory cap, placeholder overwrite path, Submitted-at-injection) — no remaining unrecorded asymmetry — and added a wiring-drift test asserting every flag the campaign constructs exists in the target script's argparse, making the T1 class of divergence a test failure instead of a mid-campaign crash. Two spec amendments applied under ratchet v2 with rationale + rejected alternatives + tripwire checks (applied_08_both_arm_budget_audit.md, applied_08_adaptive_campaign_boundary.md); neither flips anything to pass — both add obligations discharged by same-iteration work. 111 tests pass (102 post-merge + 9 new), py_compile clean, compute_metrics/tau_sweep/budget_audit re-smoke-run on the real pilot artifacts, campaign dry-run prints the correct full plan. Because this iteration found and fixed real, substantive flaws (one blocker-class), gold_standard_met is FALSE per the charter; the loop should pass once more over the unified branch.

issues_found.title: The campaign branch (the launch lineage) forked at iteration 3 and lacked all iteration-4-7 design and producer fixes, including the pro-treatment predictions bias confirmed on 5/10 pilot instances; scrutiny 6 and 7 had flagged the required rebase and it never happened
issues_found.rationale: A pre-registered design is a property of the artifact lineage that runs; launching from this branch would have produced headline artifacts violating every documented completeness guarantee. Merged review-loop/20260610-013030 in (conflict resolved by the verified-superset iteration-5+ eval driver); 102 merged tests green immediately; wiring-drift test added so this class of divergence becomes a test failure.

issues_found.title: budget_audit.py could not read the control arm's nested layout (<iid>/run<idx>/<iid>/...), so R6.3's cross-arm token comparison — the measurement behind the 'control receives at least as much compute' fairness claim — was incomputable on exactly the arm where the claim could fail; the campaign audited only the treatment while claiming both arms
issues_found.rationale: A fairness audit that can only see one arm is an assertion, not an audit. Layout auto-detection + draw records keyed by the predictions tid run<idx>; crashed resamples disclosed; budget_audit_control campaign step; both-arm commands in RESULTS SS5; R6.3 amended to require stage-tested both-arm support (applied_08_both_arm_budget_audit.md). Treatment numbers verified unchanged on the pilot.

issues_found.title: The campaign's data-reading LLM analyst was pinned to the iteration-3 design (scrutiny_03-only prompt, pre-H1/H2 vocabulary) and its adaptive scheduling of exploratory cells was undisclosed adaptive data collection, with an optional-stopping channel via the strategy_t0.7_seed2 repeat cell
issues_found.rationale: An analyst misreading the confirmatory structure steers GPU budget wrongly; an unpinned repeat draw invites 'the second run looked better.' Prompt repointed at scrutiny_07/04 with explicit reading rules (power floor, productivity diagnostic, saturation check, both-arm audits), test-pinned; R6.5 adaptive-execution boundary (first completed Phase A run = confirmatory dataset, repeats variance-only, decisions are artifacts, data-dependence disclosed in RESULTS SS2.2) (applied_08_adaptive_campaign_boundary.md).

issues_found.title: ensure_servers never verified the standing vLLM container serves the configured model; a wrong container would burn the retry budget on 404s (or, aliased, run wrong weights)
issues_found.rationale: Demonstrable-mismatch-only preflight comparing configs/branching.yaml model_name (litellm prefix stripped) against /v1/models ids; unknown sides never block, so no new flake source. Tested.

issues_found.title: The analyst subprocess runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions and only a prompt-level 'make no other changes'; an analyst edit to code/configs between phases would silently corrupt every later cell
issues_found.rationale: Prompts are not enforcement. Added a git-porcelain tree-integrity check around each analyst call allowing only campaign_decisions/ and results/ changes; anything else stops the campaign loudly. Tested including the rename case.
